cohort: The study reviewed 8132 births at a tertiary-care Portuguese hospital between 2018 and 2022 to identify and analyse neonatal clavicle fractures.
finding: The incidence of neonatal clavicle fractures was 1.1%, with instrumental vaginal birth (OR 2.072), shoulder dystocia (OR 35.71), and gestational diabetes (OR 1.761) significantly increasing the risk.
mod_finding: Vaginal births had a significantly higher incidence of clavicle fractures (1.7%) compared to cesarean sections (0.04%), and instrumental vaginal birth doubled the probability of clavicle fractures compared to spontaneous births.
